turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it, Hale. My son found out he got a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
You're welcome. Now answer the question: who entered the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.

That's a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says in writing it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student. I have their guide printed in my bag. So what else do you have, or is that the whole case?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.

"Quite reliable." Okay. Fourteen detection tools were tested last year and the researchers called them neither accurate nor reliable, and your own procedure, 4.3, says software alone doesn't establish a concern. Is there anything with a date on it, Hale, or am I going upstairs?
So I had to give him a zero.
"Had to." Procedure 4.2 says you contact the parent before any mark is entered, and you didn't, so you decided first and asked questions later. I'm writing that down.
I hope you understand my position.
Don't manage me. Your position is a software score and a skipped procedure. Withdraw the zero today, or I'm in the principal's office when we're done.
